entries.task_id: same bantu|grammar|(mous 2003a: 5-6) and differ only in lexicon
entries.description: same Bantu grammar (Mous 2003a: 5-6) and differ only in lexicon
entries.subject: same Bantu

spans.text: The two languages share one and the same Bantu grammar (Mous 2003a: 5-6) and differ only in lexicon.
The Mbugu people speak two languages: one is a mixed language and the other is a Bantu language, and the two languages share one and the same grammar and differ only in lexicon.

entries.description: Other terms are equally problematic
entries.subject: Other terms

spans.text: Other terms are equally problematic.

entries.task_id: term dialect|is|inappropriate
entries.description: term dialect is inappropriate
entries.subject: term dialect

spans.text: The two lects differ substantially in their core vocabulary and are not mutually intelligible (unless one has learned the other lexicon); moreover, the purpose of the mixed language is to create a different language; hence the term dialect is inappropriate; the term register has the wrong connotation because it suggests a choice depending on context, which is not the case as I show below.

spans.text: The inclusion of a chapter on a mixed language such as Mixed Ma’a/Mbugu in a book on pidgins and creoles is proper for several reasons.

entries.description: the language is known under the name Mbugu
entries.subject: the language

spans.text: Ma’a/Mbugu is spoken in Tanzania, where the language is known under the name Mbugu, or Ki-Mbugu with the Swahili prefix ki to indicate the language, contrasting with Wa-Mbugu for the people.

entries.task_id: one|is|a mixed language and the other is a bantu language
entries.description: one is a mixed language and the other is a Bantu language
entries.subject: one
entries.object: a mixed language and the other is a Bantu language

spans.text: The Mbugu people speak two languages: one is a mixed language and the other is a Bantu language, and the two languages share one and the same grammar and differ only in lexicon.

entries.task_id: dominant language|is|shambaa (or ki-shambaa
entries.description: dominant language is Shambaa (or Ki-shambaa
entries.subject: dominant language

spans.text: The Mbugu people live in the Usambara Mountains, where the dominant language is Shambaa (or Ki-shambaa, Sambaa, Shambala), a Bantu language (Lang-Heinrich 1921, Besha 1989, Riedel 2009).

entries.task_id: scattered and|are|not confined to certain villages
entries.description: scattered and are not confined to certain villages
entries.subject: scattered and

spans.text: In the case of the Mbugu there is the additional complication that the people live scattered and are not confined to certain villages.

entries.task_id: mbugu|originated|in kenya
entries.description: Mbugu originated in Kenya
entries.subject: Mbugu

spans.text: The scenario that I consider the most likely (see Mous 2003a) is one in which the Pre-Mbugu originated in Kenya, where they spoke an Eastern Cushitic language related to the now extinct Yaaku and to Dahalo.

spans.text: These initiation languages are parasitic on the common language and consist of an extra parallel lexicon, similar to the relationship between the mixed and the non-mixed Ma’a/Mbugu.

entries.task_id: these people|are|considered fully mbugu
entries.description: these people are considered fully Mbugu
entries.subject: these people

spans.text: The persistence of the non-mixed variety in addition to the mixed one can be explained by the fact that some Mbugu people speak only the non-mixed variety; yet these people are considered fully Mbugu.

entries.task_id: the shambaa|are|the dominant population in the usambara mountains
entries.description: the Shambaa are the dominant population in the Usambara Mountains
entries.subject: the Shambaa
entries.object: the dominant population in the Usambara Mountains

spans.text: Since the Shambaa are the dominant population in the Usambara Mountains, the Shambaa language is strong in that area and there is unbalanced multilingualism: Mbugu people speak Shambaa but not the other way around.
